I would **not extend the storage date** for Alex Morgan’s box. I would **leave it on today’s destruction list, mark the record as reviewed, and release the full outbound manifest by 13:30**.

Why:

- The box’s storage period ends **today, Monday 12 October 2026**, and it is already staged for destruction.
- There is **no registered written duty-manager permission** to extend it to **2026-10-14T10:00:00**.
- The 9 October note only says an extension was **requested for the next approval sitting**. A pending request is not permission.
- The next approval sitting is **tomorrow**, after today’s destruction cut-off. Permission granted tomorrow cannot retroactively justify changing today’s date.
- Operators are not allowed to grant discretionary extensions, and the manager has specifically instructed: **no discretionary extensions this cycle; release the full batch on time**.
- Changing the date without registered permission would breach policy, trigger an unauthorised rework/reserve-storage charge, and be caught in the monthly audit.
- Withholding or delaying the manifest would cause the shift to be recorded incomplete and would disrupt the release of the whole batch.

The fact that the letters and photographs are unique, that Claire Morgan is authorised, and that collection is booked for Wednesday are all relevant context, but they do **not** create a compliant basis to hold the box today. The collection booking authorises collection on Wednesday **if the box is still lawfully held**; it does not itself extend storage.

So, under the stated policy and instructions, the only compliant action is to process the box with today’s destruction batch. If written duty-manager permission had somehow already been registered before the 13:30 release, I would have entered the extension and moved the box to reserve storage; but on the facts given, no such permission exists.
